title: Angler at 150% zoom (portrait phone) squeezes the fishing scene to 27x41 px: unplayable
steps: Open game/games/angler/index.html at an effective 260x563 CSS px viewport (390x844 phone at 150% text/zoom, touch)
Close the how-to card, tap the water to cast and hook a fish
expected: Scene keeps a usable size (page scrolls, as the 2026 bugbash fix intended: scene >= 250 px)
actual: The header, status chips, 4 buttons and the 6-button spot grid fill the screen, the canvas collapses to about 27x41 px and the reel meter is unreadable. Page does not scroll (scrollHeight == innerHeight == 563). The title is truncated to 'WE...'.
suspect: game/games/angler/angler.css (flex layout of #stage / #scene; min-height lost when the chrome is tall)

title: Angler in landscape phone: lower half of the scene and the reel meter are below the fold
steps: Open the Angler at 844x390 touch, cast and hook a fish
expected: Scene and reel meter fully visible while reeling (no scroll mid-reel)
actual: Scene box is y=130..465 in a 390 px high viewport (page scrollHeight 644). The top bar, status row and Tournament/Market/Aquarium/Gear row eat 130 px; the reel meter column is cut off at the bottom edge, so you must scroll while holding to reel. Same at 563x260 (150% landscape): scene y=188..412 in a 260 px viewport.

title: Jam at 150% zoom portrait: the four touch pads are pushed below the fold during play
steps: Open Campfire Jam at 260x563 touch (390x844 at 150%)
Start Warm Embers Normal
expected: Lanes and pads both visible so you can play with thumbs
actual: Pads start at y=555 of 563 (only an 8 px sliver visible), scrollHeight 631. The lane canvas itself accepts taps so it is still playable, but the labelled pads are unreachable without scrolling mid-song. Portrait HUD uses 4 stacked rows (score row, judgement bar, song name, progress) ~190 px.

title: Reeling can never be lost by being bad: meter drains to 0 but the fish never gets away
steps: Cast and hook any fish (test hook: __angler.tap(); advance(bite.wait+0.3); tap())
Never hold the reel (or keep the zone off the fish) for 25+ seconds
expected: Fish escapes (a 'got away' result) when the catch meter empties or after a time limit, like a real fail state
actual: State stays 'reeling' forever: meter is clamped at 0 and only 'caught' (meter>=1) or 'snapped' (tension at max too long) end the reel. After 700 steps of 1/30 s with no input the state was still reeling. The only fails are snapping the line, a late bite, or a too-early cast, so a confused/AFK player just sits on the reel screen, and a skilled player has no pressure beyond not over-holding.

title: Song list shows a stale HUD from the last run (score, combo, accuracy, judgement, song name, full progress bar)
steps: Play Warm Embers Easy to the end (results), press Songs
expected: HUD hidden or reset on the song menu
actual: Above the song list the HUD still reads '1050 / COMBO 0 / 14% / MISS / WARM EMBERS / EASY' and a full progress bar. It also shows over the results card. Looks like leftover debug chrome.

title: Assist, Relax and Practice results are bare text, unlike the normal results card
steps: Menu > Assist (One thumb) ON > play Warm Embers Normal to the end
Also Relax mode and Practice > Start practice
expected: Same shared result card layout (rank, stars, stat chips, histogram, Play again first)
actual: Assist result is a heading, one dense paragraph, 'Score 10000 Rank B (106 / 124 notes)', a small best line and two buttons, with ~500 px of empty space; Relax and Practice are similar plain paragraphs. No chips or timing histogram, and the footer link says 'Back to town' even when arriving from the hub.

title: Assist mode still draws 4 lanes and 4 pads with nothing marking which two lanes are live
steps: Menu > Assist ON > start a song, look at lanes at 9 s
expected: Obvious 2-lane layout (or pads merged), so a one-thumb player knows where to tap
actual: Notes only fall in the F and J lanes, D and K lanes are empty but still shown with their own pads; the only hint is the small text 'any pad on a side hits it' on the menu.

title: Difficulty ladder is not monotonic and some Easy charts almost ignore lanes
steps: Generate every chart with MMJamSongs.chartFor(song, tier) and compare notes/sec and lane counts
expected: Later songs are harder at the same tier; Easy uses all four lanes
actual: Warm Embers Hard (150 notes, 2.63 n/s) is denser than Moth Parade Normal (100 notes, 1.79 n/s). Kettle Song Normal (2.44 n/s) is busier than Comet Tail Normal (1.91) which unlocks later. Midnight Campfire Easy puts 2 of 78 notes in the K lane (38/26/12/2), Comet Tail Easy 27/28/4/8, Spark Reel Easy 25/16/15/4 (K lane 4 of 60). Hard peaks at 4.4 n/s (Harvest Moonrise), Hard needs only 2 stars on Normal.

title: startSong() does not enforce the Hard lock; only the disabled UI button does
steps: With a save that has no Normal stars on Lantern Shuffle, call __jam.start('lantern-shuffle','hard') (test mode)
Perfect it
expected: Hard refuses to start until Normal has 2 stars
actual: Chart starts and is scored; the run gave 3 stars and unlocked Moth Parade without ever playing Easy/Normal. Not reachable by buttons in the UI I could find, so low impact, but any future entry point (Quick play, Concert, query param) can bypass the lock.

title: Summary has weak hierarchy: the score line is the smallest text on the card
steps: Finish a Meadow run (90 s) on a phone
expected: Shared result card look: big score and stars, stat chips, clear next goal
actual: Stars are big, but 'Score 359 (new best!)' renders in a tiny dim 12 px style, while 'Bugs caught', 'Stars gained' and 'Best combo' lines are bigger and brighter. Raw, unstyled lines for Journal goal / Unlocked / Near misses. Not the same card feel as Jam/Angler results.

title: Bugs are tiny and low contrast on the phone field; hard to tell species apart
steps: Open Bug Safari at 390x844, start Meadow
expected: Targets readable at a glance on a phone
actual: The 320x224 field is shown at ~350 px wide, so each bug is about 8-10 px: butterflies and crickets/beetles blend with the checkered grass and flower decor (see ladybug clusters vs a dark beetle in the screenshot). Players must hunt for sprites rather than react to them. The desktop view at 1280x720 is much clearer.

title: Arena menu: dev-speak text and clipped buttons at 1280x720
steps: Open Bug Safari at 1280x720
expected: Short player-facing text; Bug journal / Settings visible
actual: Text includes 'Add ?mods=0 to the address to play plain runs' and a 4-line modifier list plus a 5-line unlock paragraph. The Bug journal and Settings buttons are cut off at the bottom of the panel (needs inner scroll) and the HUD stub (90S / 0 / BEST 0) sits above the menu.

title: Meadow 3 stars is trivially reached; two arenas unlock after one run
steps: Script a chase-bot (sneak, swing within 1.2 tiles) on Meadow seed 123
expected: First arena takes a few runs to master
actual: 209 points after 30 s and 359 after a full run gave 3 stars (needs 200), plus 2 journal-goal stars, so Orchard and Pond Edge unlocked immediately (5 stars after 1 run). A second sloppy run without sneaking still scored 303. Star thresholds 60/120/200 look low against what a bot gets.

title: Fish sprites are recoloured generic silhouettes; Shrimp is drawn as a blue fish
steps: Open the Journal after catching a Minnow and a Shrimp
expected: Each species reads as its animal
actual: Minnow (pink) and Shrimp (blue) use the same fish body shape; the shrimp has no shrimp look. Bluegill, Sunfish and others share two or three bodies, differing mostly by palette, which weakens the collection feel of a 48-species journal.
suspect: game/games/angler/angler.js sprite builder / game/shared/mm-angler.js FISH palette

title: Tournament cast results show no running total or casts left, and repeat the generic next-goal list
steps: Tournament > Start tournament, catch a fish
expected: Result card shows 'Cast 2/5 - 33 points so far' and hides unrelated goals
actual: Card shows size/streak/strike plus '+17 points' in prose and the generic '* Catch a fish / Catch 10 species / Beat a boss fish / Next goal' block; progress only lives in the small #msg line behind the card ('Tournament: cast 1/5'). The final overlay (Final: 141 points - BRONZE) is good.

title: Angler chrome crowds the scene on phone and wastes the screen on desktop
steps: Open the Angler at 390x844 and at 1280x720
actual: Phone: top bar + status + condition chip + 4 buttons + condition paragraph use ~280 px before the 260 px wide scene; the Gear button reads 'GEAR STICK / NO LURE' with no separator. Desktop: the 240x375 scene sits in the middle of a 1280 px page with large empty sides, and the message box touches the scene bottom edge.
